reason: Clearing wound debris seems like a useful first step toward repair.
expectation: Phagocytes will clear some debris around the sealed wound, though other repair processes will still be needed.

alternatives.reason: Growing the blood supply also supports repair, but I chose to address debris first.

effect: Debris is cleared, and the wound now needs supply, surface and support.
reaction: The three empty slots make the remaining repair tasks clear.
reason: Repair signals acting on the nearby capillary should help establish a blood supply for the wound.
expectation: I expect the capillary to form a growing vessel or supply route, though it may need another step to connect it to the wound.

alternatives.reason: Starting collagen production would address support, but I chose the supply route first.

effect: The repair signals produced a capillary sprout connected to the existing circulation, ready to add to the wound.
reaction: The growing branch makes the supply route easy to follow.
reason: Fit the capillary sprout into the healing wound to advance its supply.
expectation: I expect the wound's supply slot to be filled, with the new vessel helping supply the repair site.

alternatives.reason: Starting the fibroblast RNA route would address support, but I prefer to finish the supply connection first.

effect: The capillary sprout now forms a connected flow route supplying the wound; surface and support remain.
reaction: The completed vessel loop makes the supply connection clear.
reason: Start the fibroblast RNA pathway to build support for the wound.
expectation: I expect fibroblasts to make RNA messages for repair proteins, with further steps needed to produce the supporting matrix.

alternatives.reason: Closing the surface also matters, but I chose to begin the support route first.

effect: The fibroblasts have made collagen messenger RNA, ready for protein production.
reaction: The DNA-to-RNA connection is clear, though it repeats an earlier chapter's pathway.
reason: Add matrix nutrients to continue the wound-support pathway.
expectation: I expect the fibroblasts to use the amino acids and RNA instructions to make collagen or supporting matrix.

alternatives.reason: Surface closure also remains, but I want to continue the support pathway first.

effect: The fibroblasts produced and exported collagen fibres, creating connective tissue ready to support the wound.
reaction: The sequence clearly links the RNA instructions to extracellular collagen.
reason: Fit the new connective tissue into the healing wound to provide support.
expectation: I expect the support slot to be filled, while the surface still needs closing.

alternatives.reason: Surface closure is also needed, but I want to finish the support route first.

effect: The wound now has collagen-rich support, though the young tissue is not yet as strong as uninjured skin; surface closure remains.
reaction: The qualification about the tissue's strength adds useful context.
reason: This is the only offered combination and should advance surface closure.
expectation: I expect the nourished epidermal cells to grow or move across the wound, possibly needing another step to fit the new surface.
